claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure with multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A physics-informed multiscale neural network can integrate stacking-fault energies, short-range-order parameters, and hierarchical-morphology descriptors.
Sparse training on first-principles data and coarse thermophysical or CALPHAD estimates will permit rapid, accurate mechanical-property prediction for hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
The hierarchical heterostructure and its local chemical fluctuations mediate elastic behavior.
The hierarchical heterostructure and its local chemical fluctuations mediate fracture behavior.
Physically meaningful local descriptors allow the neural network to bridge atomic-scale interactions and mesoscale mechanical responses.
The proposed framework reduces reliance on full-scale high-fidelity simulations.
Heterogeneous local chemical order affects dislocation movement.
Heterogeneous chemical order and microstructural morphology control crack propagation.
The approach will reduce overall simulation time by at least 50%.
The approach will reduce yield-strength prediction error by approximately 20–30% relative to traditional full-scale CALPHAD or first-principles methods.
The approach will reduce toughness prediction error by approximately 20–30% relative to traditional full-scale CALPHAD or first-principles methods.
The approach will provide Young's-modulus accuracy comparable to traditional methods.
First-principles and molecular-dynamics calculations are computationally time-consuming and difficult to use at high throughput.
CALPHAD can require significant computational resources and can be limited by incomplete databases for high-entropy alloys.
Standalone machine-learning predictions depend strongly on the size and composition of the training dataset.
The model may become unreliable when phase segregation, processing routes, or composition produce local environments outside the training regime.
Previous hybrid models support the projected efficiency and error-reduction gains.
Quantitative predictive performance will vary with the quality and representativeness of the training data.
